messages:
rachel (sales): Quick sync with infra on EchoHealth reserved proposal — they pushed back on the 25% headroom. Need a concrete alternative we can present to their finance/legal by EOD.

alex.k (infra): Ok. What does EchoHealth expect for burst? continuous 99th pct latency SLO? or just throughput guarantees?

eva - EchoHealth: hi all — want predictable 99p latency under steady 600 reqs/min baseline, plus Q4 spike handling (we anticipate ~2.5x traffic for 2 weeks). Finance wants no more than 18% uplift on committed monthly cost.

jia (capacity): Numbers first: their current plan is 1200 GPU-hours/month committed on g5-like instances, target p99 < 250ms for generation (70B quantized 4-bit). For 2.5x spike, peak demand ~3000 GPU-hours/day if naive. But batching + KV cache reduces that ~3x.

matt (runtime): Our telemetry says for 70B-4bit batch size 16 we get ~12 tokens/sec per GPU on avg; p99 is sensitive to seq len. If they stick to short responses (<=128), p99 180-240ms with proper batching.

alex.k (infra): Proposal: change the static 25% headroom to a hybrid policy: baseline headroom = max(12% of committed, 100 GPU-hours) + seasonal multiplier for known spikes. For occasional short bursts allow elastic burst up to 50% of committed for <=72 hours with a 1.15x cost uplift. That keeps avg uplift below 18% if spikes are short.

rachel (sales): Can you show a worked example I can send to them? They asked for a clear daily/monthly math table.

jia (capacity): Example (strings only): committed = 1200 GPU-hours/mo. baseline_headroom = max(0.12*1200,100) = max(144,100)=144. monthly_reserve = 1200+144 = 1344 GPU-hours. If they trigger a 72h burst at +50% of committed, additional = 0.5*1200*(72/720) = 0.5*1200*0.1 = 60 GPU-hours. So billable = 1344+60 = 1404. Uplift = (1404-1200)/1200 = 17% -> within finance ask.

eva - EchoHealth: This looks promising. Two questions: 1) what happens if region capacity constrained (we need us-east-1 only)? 2) what are SLA credits if you miss the p99 during our spike window?

alex.k (infra): 1) Region constraint: we can reserve in us-east-1 only but bump on-call and recommend a reservation across two AZs in region. If AZ outage, cross-region failover is possible but will require model cold-start and extra cost. 2) SLA: suggest standard reserved SLA with credits capped at 5% monthly invoice for missed latency targets; for burst windows we propose lowered credit multiplier (because burst is best-effort) — put explicit fallbacks: auto-route to hosted multi-region pool (no credits) or degrade to smaller model with same commit (credit policy only if we fail dedicated pool).

matt (runtime): Implementation note: bursting to hosted pool requires plan in routing policy:
```yaml
burst_policy:
  enabled: true
  max_burst_pct: 50
  max_burst_duration_hours: 72
  cost_multiplier: 1.15
  fallback: hosted_multi_region_pool
  sla_credit_on_failure: false
```

ops-bot: Deployment check: us-east-1 dedicated pool (echohealth-resv-1200) has current headroom 9% on our capacity graph; adding 12% baseline will allocate additional 144 GPU-hours from available cluster. Projection: 30% chance we need to re-imbalance other reserved pools this quarter.

jia (capacity): Risk callouts: if Q4 spike lasts >72h or repeated bursts, uplift exceeds 18% quickly. Also, preemptible/spot alternatives save ~20% but no SLA — not acceptable for their compliance. Network egress: their models output embeddings for third-party analytics, estimate additional $1.2k/mo egress cost at scale — include as separate line item.

rachel (sales): I'll craft the term sheet with: committed 1200 GPU-hrs/mo, baseline headroom formula, burst clause (50% for <=72h at 1.15x), cross-AZ only in-region failover, SLA credits cap 5% monthly, hosted fallback with no credits, explicit egress pass-through.

eva - EchoHealth: ok please add a clause for one paid trial burst (up to 72h) during onboarding so we can validate performance.

alex.k (infra): Fine by us — one onboarding trial burst as a one-time waive of the cost multiplier. We'll flag capacity and put an ops runbook.

matt (runtime): I'll prepare a short runbook snippet to attach (warmup sequences, KV cache priming, recommended batch size). Example commands to warm cache:
```bash
# synthetic warmup for 70B model
for i in {1..200}; do curl -X POST https://redwood/api/gen -d '{"prompt":"warmup","length":64}'; done
```

rachel (sales): Great. I'll send this to EchoHealth and loop back with their legal. Any objections to the numbers?

alex.k (infra): None. Just note: if they also ask for EU residency we'll need a separate commit and higher uplift due to lower pool density.

ops-bot: Note created: #INC-2026-echohealth-reserve-plan. Assigned to alex.k and jia.

eva - EchoHealth: thanks everyone, super helpful. rachel please send over and we'll review with finance. :thumbsup:

rachel (sales): Will do. Closing this thread once terms accepted. :eyes:
